gaps.what: the address of every service-to-service call is http://${X_API_ADDR}: the host is an environment variable whose value is in a ConfigMap (service-api-config), so the join of a call to a route holds only by method and path plus that manifest; with src/ledgermonolith/config.yaml the same calls of the frontend reach the monolith

three of the frontend's calls (balance, history, contacts) are built as ApiRequest objects in home() and sent by ApiCall.make_call in api_call.py through a thread pool: the caller of the route is the line that builds the URL, the HTTP call is elsewhere

the path of a call ends with a value (account id, username): /balances/{account_id} joins /balances/{accountId}, /contacts/{username} joins /contacts/<username>, each framework with its own placeholder syntax

GET /transactions/{accountId} is offered by transactionhistory and POST /transactions by ledgerwriter: the same prefix in two services, told apart only by method and by the variable that holds the host (HISTORY_API_ADDR, TRANSACTIONS_API_ADDR)

/ready, /version and /healthy exist in several services (and /login in frontend and userservice): a call to one of them joins only the service whose address it uses; joining by path alone links services that never talk
userservice, contacts and frontend define their routes as functions nested in create_app(): the handlers are not module-level symbols

the Java services are wired by Spring: controllers, repositories, the JWT verifier, the caches and RestTemplate are injected by type, the repositories are interfaces whose queries Spring Data generates, and the database address comes from SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL with no line of code that reads it

balancereader and transactionhistory learn about new transactions by polling the table in a background thread started in the controller's constructor, whose callback is a lambda: no call joins ledgerwriter to them, only the table

ledgerwriter, balancereader, transactionhistory and ledgermonolith each have their own copy of Transaction, TransactionRepository, JWTVerifierGenerator and LedgerReader with the same names: a link between the copies is false

redirects name a function with url_for: url_for('login') and url_for('consent') name the POST handlers, and the browser's GET reaches login_page and consent_page; there is no endpoint named login_page for /login POST
the template variable platform_name is never passed to render_template (the code passes platform): the test {% if platform_name is not none %} is on an undefined value

the JWT is verified with a public key file whose path is PUB_KEY_PATH and whose content is a Kubernetes secret (jwt-key): that the key userservice signs with and the key the others verify with are a pair is not in the code; the secret files were not opened
the frontend's decode_token reads claims without verifying the signature; verify_token does the check. The cookie is set without Secure or HttpOnly

the OAuth client that calls /login?response_type=code and receives the POST at redirect_uri is outside the repository (extras/apigee describes one): the caller is configured by the optional ConfigMap oauth-config
the Kubernetes Ingress and load balancer call the frontend from outside; the user's browser is the caller of every page route
kubernetes-manifests/ is generated from src/*/k8s by docs/releasing/make-release.sh (skaffold render): the same Deployments twice, with pinned images

which overlay is live (development with in-cluster Postgres StatefulSets, staging and production with Cloud SQL through cloud-sql-proxy on 127.0.0.1) depends on the Skaffold profile: the database a service reaches is decided at deploy time
Bootstrap Material Design, Popper, jQuery and the fonts come from CDN URLs in the shared templates, not from a manifest
the ui tests have no package.json: Cypress comes from the base image cypress/included

run_and_observe needs the whole system up: two databases, the key pair, six services; tracing and metrics export need Google Cloud credentials and the metadata server (ENABLE_TRACING and ENABLE_METRICS can turn them off)

Cloud Build triggers, Cloud Deploy pipelines and targets, GKE clusters, Cloud SQL instances and Artifact Registry are declared in Terraform (iac/) with variables and registry modules: what exists is known only in a real project

extras/ (apigee, asm-multicluster, backup, cloudshell, cloudsql, cloudsql-multicluster, istio, jwt, metrics-dashboard, postgres-hpa, prometheus, tls-*) are optional samples and alternative manifests, not part of the default deployment; docs/ is documentation
src/accounts/accounts-db/initdb/1-load-testdata.sql holds the same demo rows as 1-load-testdata.sh but is not copied into the image
ledger-db's 1_create_transactions.sh skips the demo data only when USE_DEMO_DATA is empty (the test uses && where accounts-db compares with True)
frontend has no unit tests: its skaffold test stage runs pylint only, and the end-to-end Cypress suite is its test
